articleTitle: Finite-Set Model Predictive Control and p-q Theory Applied on Shunt Active Filter in an Off-Grid Microgeneration System
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper deals with a finite-set model predictive control applied to a shunt active power filter. The instantaneous power theory is used to generate the compensation signals and reduce the execution time of the algorithm, which allows increasing the sampling frequency used since this is a critical condition for the type of controller considered. The model predictive control presents good transient response and tracking of high-frequency reference signals. This enables the proposed control algorithm to drive a shunt active filter in a three-phase four-wire off-grid microgeneration system under nonlinear loads. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and good performance obtained with the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Network Reconfiguration and Distributed Generators Allocation and Sizing Using Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The increment of losses can increase the operating costs and degrade the quality of power network distribution. The integration of renewable energy sources based on Distributed Generators (DGs) is one of the tools that can be used to operate distribution networks efficiently and have several technical benefits in distribution systems. However, these benefits require their installation in the proper locations with suitable sizes. Another approach that can be used to ensure efficient network operation is the network reconfiguration. The network reconfiguration is regarded as an operational approach for minimizing power losses. Thus, in this paper, two multi-objective optimization methods are used to reconfigure the distribution system and simultaneously allocate and size DGs to reduce power losses and investment costs, while respecting the operational constraints of the system. In this study, the adopted optimization methods were the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II and Strength Pareto Evolutionary Algorithm 2. The IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus test networks were used to evaluate the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Power Smoothing in Condominium Microgrids ConGRID case study
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper discusses power smoothing in a Condominium Microgrid (ConGRID). The study considers using a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) for power smoothing and its impact on distributed load and distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation. The microgrid under study, ConGRID, is located in a condominium in Barão Geraldo, Campinas, Brazil, and consists of real consumers with PV generation installed on their houses and a BESS connected at the point of common coupling. The paper provides a methodology for simulating power smoothing at ConGRID using OpenDSS, an electric grid simulator, using Simple Moving Average (SMA). The simulations were carried out using Python programming language with the support of the Google Colab environment. Results show that using the BESS for smoothing the distributed PV generation using an aggregated profile increases the power and voltage oscillations in the point of common coupling. However, when the smoothing algorithm uses the power at the distribution transformer as the reference, the strategy benefits the power system, reducing power and voltage oscillations between ConGRID and the main grid.

articleTitle: Thermal Experimental Evaluation of a Power Transformer Under OD/OF/ON Cooling Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Power transformers are extremely important for electrical systems and its internal temperatures rule the equipment lifespan. To keep the operation under safe conditions, with temperatures below the limits from standards, a cooling system must be designed to ensure the correct heat transfer to the external environment. The internal circulation of cooling system can be by natural-oil, forced-oil or directed-oil, each one with its characteristics. This study presents an experimental comparison of the thermal performance of a prototype transformer operating with the three cooling modes. A set of 22 optical fiber sensors along the HV windings, top oil and radiator inlet, and a thermal camera make possible to observe the temperature distribution along the transformer and to identify the effects of each cooling mode, providing valuable information for thermal design of more reliable transformers.

articleTitle: Project and Implementation of a Discretized Didactic System in W’ Plan Using Arduino Uno
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper shows how to implement a didactic control system to obtain zero steady-state error for a ramp input. This system could be used in situations where it is necessary to follow a specific speed profile, such as elevators. Considering that the mechanical pole is responsible for the temporal response, a DC motor can be represented by a first-order system. In this paper, a capacitor and a resistor are used to emulate the characteristics of a DC motor. An Arduino Uno is used to implement two discrete integrators to obtain zero steady-state for a ramp input. Using Bode Diagrams in W’ plane is designed a compensator. The system is assembled and tested and the results are shown.

articleTitle: Modelling and Control of an Isolated SEPIC With Voltage Multiplier Cell for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The use of high step-up converters is necessary for photovoltaic applications with microinverters, due to the low voltage of the modules, that has to be increased to the input of the inverter. In this work, an isolated dc-dc high step-up SEPIC with a Greinacher voltage doubler cell is used for this. Due to the continuous input current, high voltage gain, isolation, high efficiency and use of a single switch, it is a suitable and attractive converter for this application. In order to present the modelling and control, the dynamic model of the converter is obtained using the state-space averaging technique. For the control strategy, a Proportional Integral (PI) is used with the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) to regulate the input voltage of the PV module. Simulation results are presented to validate the obtained model, while closed-loop experimental results on a 50 kHz, 310 W prototype are presented to validate the proposed concept.

articleTitle: On the selection of classical advanced controllers for TISO systems
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: José Diogo Forte de Oliveira Luna

abstract: There are basically three approaches regarding classical advanced controllers for TISO systems, these being adopting independent controllers, split-range control, and mid-ranging control (also known as valve position control). Despite the recent attention that has been devoted to improving such classical strategies, there is a lack of a systematic method for choosing the appropriate control approach for a given TISO system. Aiming to address this issue, the present paper provides insights and recommendations for selecting classical advanced controllers for TISO (two-input, single-output) systems in process control, by presenting a novel decision scheme. The study also presents illustrative examples of the three strategies and argues in favor of the validity of the proposed decision method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Real Time Implementation of Resampling Schemes: An Approach Based on IEC 61850-9-2
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Signal resampling is a signal processing technique with several applications, among them to improve Sampled Values (SV) signals defined by IEC-61850-9-2. This makes it possible to analyze the SV signal more accurately and robustly for power substation protection. In this sense, this work aims to analyze and compare different resampling schemes, to validate them and explore their advantages. For this, schemes proposed by the literature and using conventional methods are analyzed. In addition, the schemes are implemented in a simulating signal (SV current) considering the signal as a whole and in a real time implementation. From the analyzes carried out, it can be seen that the resampling using the conventional Cubic Spline method presented one of the best performances, considering computational efficiency, spectral leakage, frequency variations and RMS measurements.

articleTitle: Power Quality Parameters as Energy Performance Indicator of Buildings with Photovoltaic Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Rogério Diogne De Souza e Silva

abstract: The electricity distribution system is going through a period of great transformations, arising from several factors from technological advances to regulatory changes, changing the traditional relationships between customers, energy market, and operators of distribution systems. Among the technological factors, distributed energy resources (DERs) stand out, which, in addition to being a good operational and economic alternative, contextualizes and contributes to the energy transition scenario. In Brazil, distributed generation, especially photovoltaic, is expanding significantly, adding the power customer to the role of supplier of excess energy to the electrical grid. In this context, this work is situated, considering photovoltaic generation and energy efficiency as distributed energy resources, customer units in two different parts of the country were used as a living laboratory, one in the semi-arid region of the Brazilian Northeast and the other in the Center region West with tropical climate, both with excellent values of direct normal irradiation, but with temperature variations throughout the year, providing the comparison and analysis of the behavior of the installed load and photovoltaic generation, through the determination of energy performance indicators. Parameters of power and energy, total and individual harmonic distortion, direct normal irradiance, and ambient temperature were used as study variables to characterize and correlate both with the performance of distributed generation and with energy efficiency actions in air conditioning. Energy performance indicators (EnPI) are mainly used in energy management systems, however, this work deals with the extrapolation of their application, to contribute to the operational and market areas, considering scenarios of use of multiple distributed energy resources, in which through the indicators it becomes possible to quantify and compare the performance between these resources.

articleTitle: Non-pulsating Input and Output Transformerless Three-Port DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In this paper is proposed a non-isolated three-port DC-DC converter (TPC) intended for connection between panel, battery, and load. The proposed converter presents a relatively simple circuit with the use of few components, and low complexity of operation. The proposed topology was analyzed theoretically, and simulated, and a prototype was built in the laboratory to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Methodology for detecting Non-Technical Losses with Smart Metering employing Multi-Agent Sytems
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article presents a methodology for detecting non-technical losses based on multi-agent systems. The agents were developed in the JADE framework. The test system was implemented in real-time mode in the HYPERSIM software. The results show that the multi-agent system correctly assists in automatic electricity theft detection.

articleTitle: Modal Identification of Power Oscillations with Continuous Wavelet Transform Applied to the Signal from the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Power Plant Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This work presents the application of the Continuous Wavelet Transform employing the complex Morlet mother wavelet for the modal identification of electromechanical transients. The observed oscillations are decoupled into simpler oscillatory modes through analytical expressions, from which the relative oscillation frequencies are estimated for each mode. Additionally, the most influential modes in the detected transient are identified based on the amplitude of each oscillation. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the method, two simulations were conducted: one using a synthetic multimodal signal and the other using a unimodal signal obtained from tests on the Power System Stabilizer of a generator from the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Power Plant.

articleTitle: Loss-of-Field Protection Testing: Software and Hardware-in-the-Loop Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents the process of modeling and testing of the ANSI 40 protection function in real-time. The model was implemented in Typhoon HIL Control Center, a simulation toolchain by Typhoon HIL, Inc. The implementation was executed in software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL). In the HIL test, the device under test (DUT) is the IED model SEL-300G. The HIL Connect amplifier coupled to the HIL 604 real time simulator is used for the secondary level tests. The goal of this paper is to present different ways to test protection functions, according to the real need.

articleTitle: Lead-acid Batteries Monitoring System Applied to Off-grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper discusses the estimation of the State of Charge, State of Health, and Remaining Useful Life prediction in battery-based energy storage systems, focus on individual electric generation systems with intermittent sources that use lead-acid batteries in stand-alone power systems. An improved Coulomb Counting approach is proposed for State of Charge estimation, resulting in an average and maximum error of 1.9% and 2.97%, respectively, ensuring reliability in the system monitoring. The evaluation of Coulomb Counting in specific element voltage ranges, applied to determine the State of Health, has proven capable of detecting degradation even after a battery element replacement. Linear regression techniques were employed to determine the degradation curves of the elements, providing precise projection of the end of life, with an error of only 3 cycles compared to the reference values, allowing accurate prediction when replacing battery elements up to 120 days in advance. These estimates of battery state parameters enable maximizing energy efficiency, reducing maintenance costs, and minimizing environmental impacts.

articleTitle: Assessment of controller output saturation in dynamic systems: a case of performance, efficiency and system stress trade-off
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper aims to assess the impact of incorporating limitations into the controller output. The study is conducted on a proportional-derivative controller (PD) applied in the stabilisation of an inverted pendulum system. The findings indicate the presence of a trade-off relationship between the limit imposed, the power of the control output, actuator stress and system performance. It’s discussed how the power of the control actions changes with the limitation, presenting a threshold for stability. A relation between limit percentage and oscillation amplitude is also discussed. The findings may help to better understand the trade-off relation between actuator stresses, stability and power consumption, given it’s direct relation to the controller output. It can also aid in to assess the implications of saturation on real world systems. As a secondary effect, the limitation proposed can also be presented as a simple method to change the system behaviour with only one parameter change, without changing the gains of the controller.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of L and LCL Filters in Grid-Connected Converters Regarding Volume and Losses
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This study compares the volume and losses of L and LCL filters in grid-connected converters. Optimized filter designs are analyzed for different switching frequency (15 kHz to 100 kHz) and power ratings (500 W to 10 kW). The objective is to identify the points where each filter topology is the best in terms of volume and losses. While the prevailing literature commonly suggests that the LCL filter is expected to outperform the L filter, particularly in terms of volume, the findings of the present study challenge this notion. This was possible because of the consideration of the technological limitations of the materials used in the construction of the inductors. It is shown that for some switching frequencies and power levels, the L filter presents better performance than the LCL filter, both in terms of volume and losses.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of Non-Isolated DC-DC Converters for PV System Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This work proposes an optimization methodology for the design and comparison of the basic non-isolated power converters. The non-isolated boost, buck-boost, and buck converters are evaluated. The designs are carried out considering component optimization techniques, with objective functions including efficiency, cost, and volume. The design is performed according to the mission profile of photovoltaic generation. Each converter is designed to a specific voltage and power range, according to the number of panels used in series. In the analysis, the boost converter presented greater flexibility in panel utilization, offering a wider operating range compared to the buck and buck-boost converters. Furthermore, in optimized designs, the boost converter demonstrated the best cost and power density compared to the buck-boost and buck converters.

articleTitle: Analysis of scenarios for repowering wind farms – a case of study for Uruguay
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In Uruguay, wind capacity forms a significant part of the country's energy matrix; most of the wind turbines that are currently operating were installed between 2014 and 2017, a time in which the technology for wind generation has evolved significantly, so it is analyzed how viable it is to continue operating with old wind turbines. In this study, the energy evaluation is carried out for the possible replacement of wind turbines in two wind farms in Uruguay, Park A, installed less than ten years ago, and Park B, installed more than ten years ago.For this, a study of the energy currently generated by these parks is carried out, and of the energy that could be generated after the repowering of these parks, or their replacement, maintaining the total energy of the park.The results show that in Park B, it would be convenient to carry out an in-depth economic and technical study that raises the total repowering of this park.The same results were not obtained in Park A, because its turbines are still operating satisfactorily, and its technology has not yet aged.

articleTitle: Analysis of Core Losses in a Three-Phase Distribution Transformer Under Reverse Power Flow Using the Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Photovoltaic generation is rapidly expanding, especially in small-scale residential and commercial installations, also known as distributed photovoltaic generation. An important aspect of this energy source is its intermittent generation. Power can only be injected into the grid when the solar panels are exposed to sunlight. Thus, a novel power flow pattern has emerged within the grid, in which excess generation results in a reverse power flow, that goes through the transformer towards high voltage. To attain a deeper comprehension of this phenomenon’s impact on the distribution transformer, particularly in relation to its core losses, this study develops a methodology that includes the analysis of balanced reverse power flow scenarios. Additionally, a simulation model is developed using the Finite Element Method in Ansys Electronics® software, and the results are analyzed. Based on this analysis, it can be concluded that reverse power flow increases core losses in the transformer compared to conventional power flow, although this effect is highly dependent on the equipment characteristics.

articleTitle: Random Forest Applied to Mass Imbalance Classification in Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Current predictive maintenance techniques are able to estimate when an equipment may fail and indicate the time to perform corrective actions can be taken before the failure. The objective is to carry out the maintenance at the best time in terms of convenience and cost-effectiveness. This work is based on implementing the random forest algorithm to classify a common fault that occurs in wind turbines, which is mass imbalance. Statistical analysis and data analysis techniques were used to better classify five different failure conditions and one condition without mass imbalance using Random Forest algorithm.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Switched Capacitor DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Magnetic elements, such as inductors and transformers, have been major contributors to the volume and weight of static converters. As a result, the development of switched capacitor converters has been gaining prominence in power electronics. These converters are primarily composed of semiconductors and capacitors, leading to a significant reduction in weight and volume, along with a high power density and low electromagnetic noise emission. This paper presents a novel bidirectional switched capacitor converter topology, covering the construction of the printed circuit board and the acquisition of experimental results. The aim is to demonstrate the converter’s capability to double or halve the voltage and its bidirectional functionality and efficiency. To validate the results, a prototype was developed at the laboratory, achieving a maximum efficiency of 94.8%.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Assessment of a Five-Phase YASA Machine for Automotive Traction
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This work addresses the electromagnetic assessment of a five-phase yokeless and segmented armature (YASA) machine, specifically designed for automotive traction. First, general machine data are presented, including rated values and main dimensions. Additionally, the magnetic characteristics of the grain-oriented steel to be used in the armature core and of the magnets to be used in the machine are presented. Then, 3D finite element analyses are performed to determine the main machine parameters to be used in transient models, and induction maps are obtained to analyze the saturation levels achieved with different operating conditions. Finally, the efficiency map is obtained considering the maximum torque per ampere control strategy, which also validates the applicability of the machine in a wide range of operation in terms of torque and speed.

articleTitle: Building Segmentation in Satellite Images using U-net to Identify Non-Technical Losses
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Energy losses incur a significant challenge for utility companies annually, with non-technical losses reaching to R$ 6.3 billion in 2022. This financial burden not only impacts the bottom line but also emphasizes the pressing need for innovative solutions. Unfortunately, the current methods employed for detection are not only costly but also time-consuming. With regard to this scenario, this article aims to present the use of the U-net architecture for identifying buildings through satellite images, introducing a new approach to the network structure, originally used for biomedical image segmentation. In order to evaluate the model, we conduct systematic parameter variations. By analyzing the resulting metrics and visually inspecting the outcomes, the article highlights the significant progress achieved in building detection using U-net architecture. This proposition holds the potential to yield substantial advantages for future applications, as they can leverage the methodology outlined here to attain superior results within their respective domains. Subsequently, the segmented images will be used for analysis and classification regarding the probability of the existence of illegal connections, offering a promising pathway for enhancing loss prevention strategies within the energy sector.

articleTitle: Study and Evaluation of a Non-Isolated Topology Three-Port DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article presents a review of three-port converters (TPCs), covering their operation methods, classification, and construction features. This type of converter allows for a straightforward approach to energy processing between solar panels, batteries, and loads. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the TPC, this article presents a proposal for a new non-isolated TPC topology. The proposed converter has a low number of components, operates with simplicity, offers an attractive voltage gain, and imposes low voltage stress on the components when compared to the bus voltage at a higher voltage level. Finally, simulation results are presented to validate the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Challenges and Solutions in Managing a Real-Time Database of Monitored Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Real databases that store building detection data pose significant challenges, including handling real-time data generated by remote sensing systems and effectively analyzing large volumes of Internet of Things (IoT) sensor data. Proposed solutions involve scalable databases and detection information models, while ensuring data quality and addressing measurement errors are crucial considerations. This paper explores the management of a real database containing building detection data, focusing on real-time data acquired from remote sensing systems and IoT sensors in smart buildings. The study investigates the application of advanced data management techniques and detection information models to address scalability, fault tolerance, and consistency issues in the database. It highlights the importance of utilizing local energy consumption and PV generation data for effective energy management strategies. The research presents methodologies that incorporates easily applicable algorithms and heuristics to evaluate and manipulate real datasets from monitored buildings, enabling accurate day-ahead predictions. Additionally, machine learning algorithms are employed for forecasting purposes. Through a compelling test case, the effectiveness of the proposed methodology is demonstrated, showcasing its potential to overcome database challenges and provide valuable insights for smarter building control systems and efficient energy management.

articleTitle: Methodology for Reducing the Connection Possibilities in Transmission Network Expansion Planning
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Planning the expansion of electrical transmission networks is a large combinatorial problem that requires the analysis of too many options. This makes automation difficult and requires expert knowledge to filter out viable alternatives. This paper presents an initial methodology for reducing the number of connection possibilities based on Graph Theory, employing the concepts of degree, independent set, and dominating set. The methodology was applied in the 525 kV portion of a simplified version of the South Brazilian Transmission Subsystem, using mainly the NetworkX Python library.

articleTitle: A low-cost didactic experiment for teaching adaptive filtering for automatic control
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: José Diogo Forte de Oliveira Luna

abstract: This paper presents a low-cost didactic experiment that aims to offer a practical and efficient approach to teaching adaptive filtering in control systems. In this study, the model-free adaptive filter proposed by Fortaleza et al. is adopted to introduce the students to adaptive filtering. Both a practical experimental protocol and an application model for an Arduino UNO are developed. To validate the protocol, a low-cost motor-tachogenerator module was used and the performance of the system without filter, with a linear first-order non-adaptive filter, and with the adaptive filter are compared. The illustrative results show the conclusions students can draw from the experiment, regarding the ease of use of a model-free adaptive filter and its positive effects regarding the reduction of actuator wear. Finally, it is argued that the presented experiment meets Balchen's requirements for a good practical experiment.

articleTitle: An Overview of State Estimation for Battery Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The growth in Li-Ion battery usage for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) has amplified the need for improved Battery Management Systems (BMS) design. Parameters such as State-of-Charge (SOC), State-of-Health (SOH), and State-of-Power (SOP) are crucial for BMS. This paper provides an overview of various methods to determine these states. The estimation of SOC is fundamental, as determining other states often hinges on it. Multiple techniques are presented for state estimation. They range from empirical implementations and mathematical modeling to intricate algorithms and data-driven strategies.

articleTitle: Power Coupling Influence on Virtual Synchronous Generator Control in Grid-Forming DG Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The virtual synchronous generator (VSG) strategy has become very promising in applications of grid-forming distributed generation (DG) systems based on renewable energy sources (RES). Thus, this paper presents an impact analysis of the coupling effect between the active and reactive power flow of the DG system in the VSG controller’s dynamic performance. This analysis is based on a small-signal model describing the DG power flow transient characteristics. Based on this model, the grid impedance variation effects on the system’s critical operation point are discussed. The VSG strategy performance in different operating scenarios is assessed by means of simulation results. The obtained results reveal the effectiveness of the proposed theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A Discrete-time Robust Adaptive Second-Order Sliding Mode Controller for Grid-connected Power Systems with LCL Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson D. de Oliveira Evald

abstract: This work presents a novel discrete-time robust adaptive super-twisting sliding mode (STSM) controller, which is based on the robust model reference adaptive control theory. The controller is used to regulate the currents of a grid-connected three-phase full-bridge voltage-source static inverter with an LCL filter. The proposed control strategy provides enhanced performance to the grid-tied power system by incorporating robustness to unmodeled dynamics and the ability to handle grid uncertainties. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is validated through reliable simulation results in PSIM, which consider the inverter modulation, synchronization of the controller with the grid voltages using the Kalman filter, and grid inductance variation.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Economic Feasibility of Electric Energy Storage Between White Versus Conventional Tariffs
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Energy planning is a crucial tool in the search for planned solutions, to evaluate the behavior and performance of electrical systems. This article presents an energy planning strategy to compare the economic feasibility of electricity storage in the White Tariff versus the Conventional Tariff. In this analysis, the Homer Pro software was used to carry out simulations of a photovoltaic generation with electrical energy storage to supply a residential load of 11.25 kWh/d. The analysis considers the White and Conventional tariffs of the Rio Grande Energia (RGE) and Equatorial-PA distributors. To determine the solar radiation data, it is considered the load location in the city of Santa Maria-RS. For this research, there was progressive information about inverters, photovoltaic panels and commercial batteries in order to define the appropriate data and costs for the standard arrangement. At the end of the simulations, a comparison was made between the settings chosen by the software for Conventional and White tariffs, as well as for the different company’s prices of the tariff. The simulation results for the used example indicated that the most advantageous option for the city of Santa Maria-RS served by RGE is a photovoltaic generation connected to the grid, which presenting the lowest energy cost and the lowest Net Present Cost (NPC) over the course of a 25-year project, both for the White Tariff and for the Conventional one. However, in a scenario where the tariff value increases for Equatorial-PA, it was observed that combination of storage accompanied by the photovoltaic system and network participation would become ideal for the White tariff.

articleTitle: Microgrid Data Prediction Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The electric power system is undergoing significant changes in power generation and distribution, with an increase in prosumers contributing to the growth of distributed generation. Microgrids have emerged as a focus of global research, representing a set of mini and microgenerators, energy storage systems, and loads that can operate connected to or isolated from the main power grid. MGs enhance flexibility and security in power systems, reducing losses and improving energy supply in specific areas. Machine learning (ML) techniques, such as the Random Forest Regressor (RFR), have been increasingly utilized for data prediction in various domains, including energy markets. This research employed RFR to forecast demand, energy tariffs, wind, and solar generation in a microgrid. Data from Ontario, Canada, was collected for this purpose. The results demonstrated satisfactory performance for demand and solar generation predictions, exhibiting high accuracy with low Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). However, tariff and wind generation predictions require further investigation to improve accuracy. The ML predictions will be utilized for energy management optimization and simulation in future works. Simulations in optimizing microgrid operations, with ML techniques contribute to more effective analysis and planning in the electrical sector. The study highlights the significance of research in this area to ensure reliable and efficient operation in the evolving power system.

articleTitle: Coupled Inductor Design Algorithm for E-Type Ferrite and Toroidal Kool mμ Cores
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This research project develops two algorithms to automate the design process of coupled inductors using E-type ferrite and Kool mμ cores for power electronics applications. The algorithms consider core data from datasheets and determine the necessary parameters for designing coupled inductors. Testing of constructed inductors validates their performance at 50 kHz. The study demonstrates that the algorithms effectively design coupled inductors and pave the way for broader applications of these components in power electronics systems.

articleTitle: Modeling of charging stations for impact analysis of electric vehicles in distribution networks
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The energy transition requires innovative strategies to accommodate the growing number of electric vehicles (EVs) while harnessing the potential of distributed energy resources (DERs) for a greener future. To ensure the safe and efficient operation planning of distribution systems (DSs) and foster innovation in the electricity sector, it becomes crucial to conduct sophisticated computational analyses to study the effects of EV performance within the power grid. Therefore, the purpose of this work is to present the modeling of charging stations, as well as to study the impact of EV charging on a real distribution network. The results highlight the efficacy and versatility of the models developed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Solar Photovoltaic Carport Associated with Different Electrical Cars in the City of Curitiba, Paraná - Brazil
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The transportation sector is the main responsible for Greenhouse gas emissions. Adopting Electric Vehicles (EVs) and using Renewable energy sources in the electrification of transportation systems could be the best option for the decarbonization process. This current article presents not only the analysis of the energy production of the Solar Carport, located at the Federal University of Technology–Paraná, at Neoville Campus, but also its performance through the merit indexes. Models of EVs are also compared with the Carport consumption and a respective car model powered by combustion.

articleTitle: Battery scheduling models in smart buildings: a systematic literature review
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Economic development brings the current scenario closer to the depletion of natural resources. Directly related to this it’s the energy consumption and the need to seek sustainable solutions to prevent the harmful consequences of this depletion. Solar energy harnessed through photovoltaic technology is a solution capable of reducing the environmental impact, as it is a resource that is less harmful to the environment. The energy demand is seen as rising worldwide, and strategies must be developed to improve energy efficiency and maintain the balance of the electrical network, considering the comfort of consumers and the minimization of polluting emissions. In this sense, the concept of Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) aims to reduce electricity bills, maintain the efficiency of electronic equipment, and Demand Response, which seeks to change the use of electricity by consumers. Thus, the present study aims to search the literature for different HEMS models, specifically battery scheduling, for the future application of a model for a case study in the laboratory GECAD - Research Group on Intelligent Engineering and Computing for Advanced Innovation and Development.

articleTitle: Computational modeling of a 119 kWp photovoltaic system
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: An important aspect of medium and large photovoltaic systems is the ability to predict future electricity generation based on predicted meteorological data as well as the technical and structural characteristics of the system. This prediction can be enabled by applying mathematical models or artificial intelligence. This study aims to develop a reliable and valid computational model using measurements from a real 119 kWp photovoltaic plant at the Federal Institute of Espirito Santo. The model considers meteorological data from a solarimetric station located in the same area, as well as system losses in both AC and DC components. The results indicate that the simulated generation closely aligned with the actual figures, achieving an acceptable low percentage error, less than 0.5%, during the period from September to December 2022.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of ARIMA, LSTM, and XGBoost for Very Short-Term Photovoltaic Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) forecasting is required to optimize grid management and boost renewable energy integration. This paper presents a comparative analysis of three forecast models, autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and long short-term memory (LSTM) for very short-term PV forecasting applied to two real datasets. The main objective is to evaluate the complexity, performance, and accuracy of these algorithms in predicting very short-term PV power based only on the historical PV time series data. Furthermore, an additional study incorporates weather and calendar features for the LSTM model to examine their impact on forecasting quality. The performance of the models is evaluated in terms of root mean squared error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE). Feature selection and hyperparameter optimization are also considered. The results highlight the strengths and limitations of each forecasting model in accurately capturing very short-term PV variations and show that XGBoost had the most accurate forecasting metrics for both datasets for univariate models. The research outcomes provide valuable insights for energy system operators, grid managers, and renewable energy stakeholders to make informed decisions regarding grid stability and efficient integration of PV generation.

articleTitle: Computational Study of Dirt's Effect on Solar Panel Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a computational methodology to determine input characteristics correlated with solar power generation. Solar power can be influenced by several factors, such as dirt accumulation on the panels, temperature, irradiation, and location, which may reduce the energy generation capability. Our objective is to quantify losses in photovoltaic power generation due to dirt on the panels using a computational method that analyzes the most correlated input features with solar power generation. Data was collected from a meteorological station and a photovoltaic system located at the Federal Institute of Espirito Santo, Serra campus, Brazil, to develop a dataset. This dataset was then utilized by the computational method to ascertain the most correlated features. Consequently, we were able to evaluate the impact of dirt both when the panels were dirty and after cleaning them. We analyzed the effect of six years of dirt accumulation before cleaning the panels. Following the feature correlation analyses, we opted to use the average solar radiation and temperature readings from the LPNET14 sensor, infrared radiation, and relative humidity to study the dirt's impact. As a result, we determined that cleaning the panels led to a 4.01% increase in the system's power output.

articleTitle: Modeling and design of a low-cost constant current electronic load
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Electronic loads are very useful tools for various applications in an electronics laboratory, but their high cost and lack of precise mathematical representation in the literature is a significant limitation. In this sense, this work presents the design and modeling of low-cost direct current (dc) analog electronic load. Design recommendations are presented in terms of a comprehensive design procedure. The related equations are presented, giving a broader understanding of the principles of operation. Three distinct test scenarios are analyzed, whereas the equipment relies on low-cost components.

articleTitle: Distributed Energy Resources and Fast Charging Stations Allocation for Enhanced System Operation and Charging Infrastructure Coverage
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The growing insertion of Electric Vehicles (EVs) in the distribution system is a promising solution to mitigate the greenhouse emission issue. However, as the number of EVs significantly increases, the excessive charging demand of Fast Charging Stations (FCSs) may lead to instability problems in the distribution network. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-objective optimization approach for the allocation and sizing of Fast Charging Stations (FCSs) with the objective of minimizing their installation and operation costs, while maximizing the coverage for EVs. It is well-known that the integration of EVs results in increased power losses. As a consequence, in this study, an optimized planning of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) was also performed with the purpose of mitigating this issue. The Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) was applied to obtain the Pareto curve, which made it possible to minimize the objective functions for the 33-bus test feeder and 25-node transportation network, considering commercial and residential areas. Based on the solution selected by the Fuzzy Decision-Making method, it was possible to minimize the voltage deviation even with the insertion of the FCSs in the system.

articleTitle: Home Energy Management Systems Model Applied for Distributed Energy Resources, Multi-type Load Scheduling, and Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: As the final link in an integrated energy system of the future, the Home Energy Management System (HEMS) plays a crucial role in enabling homeowners to intelligently and conveniently manage the usage of their household appliances, renewable energy generation (RES), energy storage systems (ESS), and electric vehicles (EVs). In this article, we propose a holistic model that prioritizes user preferences when scheduling the usage of various physical devices with different characteristics. Additionally, we present a charging and discharging strategy specifically designed for ESS and EVs, taking into account their capital costs, in order to seamlessly integrate them into the HEMS framework. This integration provides increased flexibility, economic advantages, and prolonged battery life. By utilizing Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and the proposed model, we can obtain an optimized energy schedule for the smart home, ensuring both the lowest cost and user comfort. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we present an illustrative case study.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of an optimal quadratic controller with minimum order observer
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper addresses a critical need in the literature for research focused on the real-world implementation of combined optimal control strategies and minimum order observers. Despite the recognized advantages of these methods, there is a notable absence of studies that apply both techniques in tandem to naturally unstable and nonlinear systems. To address this research gap, this paper presents a detailed exploration of control systems, focusing on the design and implementation of an optimal control strategy based on the Linear Quadratic Regulator method, coupled with a minimum order observer. The methodology is systematically outlined, providing a versatile blueprint that can be utilized for a variety of high order systems. This paper also highlights the common challenge of reconciling theoretical results with real-world implementation, thereby emphasizing the complexity of transitioning control strategies from theory to practice. While the actual system’s behavior exhibits some deviations from the simulation due to inherent non-linearities, the established objectives were still successfully met, demonstrating satisfactory results. This highlights the practical applicability of the control design, despite the inherent complexities of real-world systems. This paper concludes by suggesting further exploration of optimal controllers and state observers in different types of systems, thus contributing to fill the gap within the literature underlining the use of these strategies in real-world systems.

articleTitle: Electric Forklifts: Technological Advancements and Impacts on Energy Transition and Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The article addresses the state of the art of electric forklifts, emphasizing their technological advantages in relation to traditional models. In addition, it discusses the environmental and energy benefits of these devices, presenting studies that suggest their technical and economic feasibility. The study aims to provide data and arguments to support decisions on the replacement of combustion models with electric forklifts, promoting the modernization of the industry and the adoption of more sustainable practices.

articleTitle: Allocation and Sizing of Distributed Generators in Distribution System Using Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Currently, in Brazil, the integration of Distributed Generation into the Electric Power Distribution System has become a protagonist in the expansion of the electricity supply in the country. HHowever, despite its modularity and flexibility as an energy source, improper allocation and sizing can lead to issues in the quality of supplied energy, making the distribution system unreliable. Possible flaws in the protection system, increased harmonic distortion, and elevated power losses are some of the associated issues. Thus, in this article, a multi-objective optimization method is employed to allocate and size distributed generators, aiming to reduce power losses and investment costs while respecting operational constraints of the system. In this study, the adopted optimization method was the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II, and the IEEE 37-node test network was used to evaluate the proposed methodology. The developed algorithm demonstrated its capacity and robustness in solving the optimization problem, achieving an 8% reduction in power losses with the least increase in annual investment cost compared to the original system.

articleTitle: A Comparative Evaluation of SMD and TO220 Power MOSFETs in Power Electronics Application
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This work presents a comparative evaluation of Surface Mount Device (SMD) and TO220 power MOSFETs for power electronics applications. The evaluation considers a commercial 1 kW line interactive UPS. A comprehensive database comprising 174 power MOSFETs for TO220 and SMD devices (DPAK, D2PAK, and SuperSO8) technologies is developed and used for analysis. The internal characteristics of the MOSFET technologies are compared. The cost and efficiency in full-bridge inverter used in the UPS under study is analyzed using the Pareto front. The results indicate that the SuperSO8 technology exhibits the best cost × efficiency relation. SuperSO8 and TO220 are similar in efficiency for lower-cost part numbers. Furthermore, TO220 showed better efficiency than D2PAK for lower-cost part numbers, but lower efficiency for higher-cost part numbers in Pareto front.

articleTitle: Distributed Energy Resources, Capacitor Banks and Fast Charging Stations Allocation using a Multi-Objective Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) have experienced widespread adoption as a sustainable mode of transportation, leading to a significant increase in Electric Vehicle Charging Stations (EVCSs) within the network. However, the installation of EVCSs can have a negative impact on distribution systems due to the increasing demand for EV charging. Therefore, this paper introduces a novel multi-objective optimization approach for the efficient allocation and sizing of Fast Charging Stations (FCSs), Distributed Energy Resources (DERs), and Capacitor Banks (CBs). The primary objectives are to simultaneously minimize investment and operational costs, voltage deviation, and power losses in the network. Furthermore, the methodology accounts for daily variations and uncertainties in DERs generation, load, and EVs traffic in order to ensure the optimization of the objective functions under varying network conditions. The multi-objective optimization problem is solved using Multi-objective Cuckoo Search and Fuzzy Decision-Making method. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology was demonstrated on the 33-bus test system. From the results, it was possible to reduce the voltage deviation and power losses by 14.24% and 19.02%, respectively, when compared to the original system.

articleTitle: Integration of Electric Vehicles into the Grid: Challenges and Opportunities for a Sustainable Energy System
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper aims to explore the dynamic evolution in the electrical sector, emphasizing the increasing integration and adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) as a strategic resource for energy storage and transaction in the electrical grid. In this regard, an analysis of the potential for implementing the Vehicle-to-Industry (V2Ind) technique is presented, exploring opportunities for a more flexible and innovative operation in the industry.

articleTitle: Detecting Energy Theft through Assignment of AI Detected Buildings to Registered Consumer Units: A Novel Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for detecting energy theft within the electrical network. The method utilizes satellite imagery to identify unauthorized connections by cross-referencing building rooftops with registered consumer units. Efficiently solving the assignment problem between buildings detected by AI and registered consumer units, flagging suspicious locations lacking assigned meters for prioritized inspections. Simulated tests yielded promising results, identifying a majority of illegal connections. Real data applications are presented, discussing subsequent enhancements to increase assertiveness. The method’s practical implications empower utility companies to combat energy theft, improve system efficiency, and ensure the electrical energy sector’s reliability and profitability.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Methodology to Prioritize the Replacement and Maintenance of Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Power transformers play a fundamental and costly role in the power system. Their failures can lead to a series of operational and financial losses, significantly impacting various customers. Additionally, their influence on the regulatory remuneration base is significant, and the manufacturing process for replacement involves longer delivery times. In this context, a multicriteria methodology was developed using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to classify transformers in the high-voltage distribution substation, prioritizing those in need of replacement or maintenance. The application of this methodology results in a ranking of priorities, considering the technical, economic, and regulatory aspects to which each equipment is subject. The study was conducted using a dataset of real transformers from a Brazilian power utility. The results allowed for the identification of facilities that should receive priority in investments, considering the weighting of the criteria and the input from a group of experts. It is essential to highlight that the combination of criteria weights can lead to variations in the order of importance, emphasizing the absence of an absolute criterion and underscoring the relevance of individually analyzing each transformer. The oldest transformer may not always be prioritized for replacement, as operational conditions and regulatory impact can influence the prioritization order, aiming to ensure prudent investment and the continuous supply of energy in an efficient manner.

articleTitle: Enhancing Control Systems Undergraduate Course: A Case Study of Project-Based Learning with Multiple Submissions
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper discusses the implementation of project-based learning in the Control Systems II undergraduate course at UFSM. The course focuses on digital control, modern control and design techniques, and one of the frequently encountered issues is the difficulty in achieving meaningful learning and showcasing practical applicability. To address this challenge, the course adopted project-based learning with multiple partial submissions and continuous assessment. Students were engaged in practical applications, such as designing a digital temperature controller for an aquarium and integrating heat transfer modeling. Results showed an increase in average final grades compared to a previous class without continuous assessment, indicating improved learning outcomes. Additionally, students’ feedback indicated higher motivation and consolidated knowledge through the project-based approach.

articleTitle: A Method to Improve Digital Relays Coordination in Power Systems using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The protection coordination problem presents a challenge in modern power systems. This coordination must be fast, reliable and easy to set up in order to guarantee suitable performance. This paper presents an optimization tool to determine efficient coordination between digital intelligent electronic devices (IEDs), taking into account the directional overcurrent function. Different from other research, this paper considers inverse-time overcurrent curves types (US and IEC) and discrete settings of pickup current and time multiplier as variables. To achieve this, a method based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) metaheuristic was developed. The results from a 19-bus, 11-transmission line, and 22-relay system are presented, demonstrating the effectiveness of proposed tool.

articleTitle: Real-time Condition Monitoring and Diagnostic Solution for Utility-scale Inverters and Distribution Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Due to the need to decarbonize the power industry, distributed energy resources (DER) integration and penetration are increasing annually at unprecedented levels. This decarbonization will be enabled by the connection of inverter-based DER (IBD) technologies as well as the required distribution transformers(DT) to connect the inverters to the grid. Failure of these critical equipment, namely the inverters and DT, may lead to the partial or complete loss of the DER as a source or enabler of renewable generation. This paper tests and validates a real-time condition monitoring and diagnostic solution that can be used for utility-scale inverters and DTs. The solution is based on IoT edge processing technology and cloud-based data analytics, offering ease of integration, implementation, and scalability. The data analytics estimate in real-time the severity level of the asset condition using a mathematical model of the asset combined with the extended park vector approach (EPVA). This is a generic approach that could be applied to assets owned by utilities or assets owned by developers like PV generators and battery energy storage developers. In this paper, we tested this approach on two critical assets associated with the NaS battery energy storage system (BESS): DT and inverters. NaS BESS installed at the 13 MW PV plant in Dubai. This approach is a real-time monitoring and diagnostic solution for condition-based monitoring of critical assets. This is part of the utility strategy to study the effectiveness and move towards a data-driven and predictive maintenance approach.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Management In A Microgrid For EV Fast-Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Worldwide, efforts to slow down climate change are growing, and targets for reducing CO2 emissions are mandatory. The transport sector, which is globally responsible for more than 30% of CO2 emissions, has been forced to change its fuel. Thus, the electrification of the fleet is seen as an alternative to move towards an oil-free future. Considering the significance of effectively managing energy within microgrids for sustainable energy utilization, this article focuses on the study of energy management in a microgrid designed to facilitate EV recharges along highways. Considering the generations present in the MG, the energy tariff, and the demands for recharges, an optimization problem is formulated in which the objective is to choose the (dis)charge rates of the storage present in the MG. The results showed a preference for the sale of energy from MG to the grid in periods of generation greater than the local load. The storage charging/discharging events were limited due to process losses, restrictions in the optimization problem, and because the price of energy sent to the network via the net metering system was equal to buy.

articleTitle: Analysis and Control of Voltage Levels and Power Factor in MV and LV Grids with connected PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Through the growth of photovoltaic (PV) power plants in micro and mini-generation, new control methods are needed to prevent and control the losses and hosting capacity in distribution grids. In this scenario, PV power plants connected in low-voltage (LV) and medium-voltage (MV) grids are required to control their voltages and power factor (PF) at the point of common coupling (PCC). This paper presents a simulation in OpenDSS controlled by a python code using an IEEE Test Case circuit which was modified with the insertion of PV power systems connected in the LV and MV grid, as well as some Energy Storage Systems (ESS) which are used to control the power factor and the voltage of the grid. The simulations presented are executed on a daily mode with a step size of 15 minutes. The results show the variation of the voltage in the grid without control and with different types of control, such as volt-var and volt-watt, as well as the variation of the power factor in the MV grid with unitary PF and with constant power factor mode searching for the best power factor setting at the moment. The results demonstrate the performance of different control combinations between PV Systems and ESS aiming to prevent overvoltages at the grid and achieve a better configuration of power factor.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Discrete-time Dual-Loop and Servo System Control Systems for CubeSats: An Optimized Design Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Cubesats, standardized nanosatellites, face significant challenges in attitude control due to limited energy resources. To address this issue, this study compares two discrete-time control system architectures suitable for this application: a servo system with integrator and a dual-loop controller employing a PI controller for speed and a proportional position controller. The controllers were designed to minimize an objective function directly correlated to the satellite’s energy consumption. Experimental results obtained from a prototype with a single-axis setup were compared with simulations, demonstrating that the dual-loop controller achieved a lower objective function than the servo system in the experiment. Also, the dual-loop controller was less sensitive to velocity measurement noise and dead zone effects. The findings of this study are valuable for considering the best attitude control architecture for CubeSats with restricted energy resources.

articleTitle: Analyses of Photovoltaic Systems Performance with Fuzzy Inference Systems and Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Myriam Regattieri De Biase da Silva Delgado

abstract: Renewable energy sources have been increasingly targeted as an alternative for reducing fossil fuel emissions. This scenario requires a better understanding of energy systems' performance and limitations, notably using photovoltaic setups under diverse meteorological conditions and determining device measurement uncertainties. Accordingly, this study conducts a performance evaluation of a photovoltaic system of copper, indium, and gallium (di)selenide technology. It compares the results provided by a reference normalized equation with two interpretable artificial intelligence techniques, Fuzzy Inference System and Bayesian Networks, when temperature is also considered. In the experiments, the study found significant percentage differences between the normalization procedure and the fuzzy system on days with lower irradiation values. On the other hand, the results provided by Bayesian networks presented lower difference percentages in relation to the normalization equation values.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Implementation and Commercialization Scenario of Photovoltaic Solar Energy in Brazil
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The studies related to alternative energy management with renewable sources of energy generation have been increasingly becoming a necessary and urgent agenda to address the exponential increase in energy consumption worldwide, in accordance with environmental and sustainable requirements for the sector. With one of the cleanest energy matrices in the world, Brazil has been advancing in the development of alternative energies. In addition to hydroelectric sources, which are stable in growth but still responsible for the majority of the energy generated in the country, renewable sources are growing rapidly. The proper management of the integration of distributed energy resources among consumers offers several positive aspects in terms of quality and reliability, not only for consumers but also for the distribution system and the environment. Due to the advantages related to abundance and its inexhaustible characteristic, solar energy has been gradually evolving as a good solution for alternative energy generation. In this regard, this study assesses the current situation of photovoltaic solar generation in Brazil, analyzing both technical data and data related to the commercialization and regulation of the source.

articleTitle: An Evolutionary-based Parametrization of Robust Adaptive Second-Order Sliding Mode Controller Applied on Grid-injection Control of Grid-tied Converters with LCL Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 15th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo Jefferson D. de Oliveira Evald

abstract: This work presents an evolutionary-based parametrization for a new discrete-time robust adaptive second-order sliding mode controller. The automatic design procedure is performed using a genetic algorithm. The novel controller is based on robust model reference adaptive control theory and a super-twisting algorithm. The resulting controller is applied to a grid-tied converter with an LCL filter. The proposed design approach, a meta-heuristic algorithm inspired by natural processes, aims to enhance the initial controller’s performance by automating the selection of the controller parameters. Simulation results using PSIM, including converter switching and converter synchronization, are presented to validate the effectiveness of the control strategy, showcasing improved performance in reducing initial transients and enhancing steady-state operation compared to the controller based on designer experience.
